subject: Privileged credential exposure: remediation verification plan & evidence request
messages:
From: security@nimbusbank.com (Elliot Harrow)
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@nimbusbank.com (Laura Chen)
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Pen test finding follow-up: exposed dev credentials & session logging gaps

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking our call last week. Attached to this thread is the penetration test report our vendor completed against the integration environment (see attachment pt_report_redwood_scope-nimbus_20260823.pdf). Two findings are blocking our compliance board sign-off:

1) Privileged credentials found in a development S3 bucket (identified as aws-access keys in /ops/backups). The report includes file paths and sample keys.
2) Session token reuse / insufficient session logging across the inference proxy (we saw requests with identical session ids over long durations and TTLs not enforced).

For our internal SOC2 timeline we need:
- A short remediation summary for each finding (what was changed, dates)
- Evidence that secrets were rotated and unused keys revoked (logs, revocation timestamps, rotation runbook)
- Logging/proof that session tokens are now short-lived and that session events are being ingested into your centralized observability (sample logs or a signed S3 object)

Can you provide an ETA and plan for delivering the evidence artifacts? Our compliance meeting is on 2026-09-22 and we need artifacts uploaded to the shared Drive by then if possible.

Thanks,
Elliot Harrow
Security Engineer
Nimbus Financial

Attachment: pt_report_redwood_scope-nimbus_20260823.pdf (PDF, 2.4MB)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: security@nimbusbank.com (Elliot Harrow)
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pen test finding follow-up: exposed dev credentials & session logging gaps

Elliot —

Appreciate the clear callout and the report. Short answer: prioritizing both findings and can deliver a verification package ahead of your compliance meeting. High-level plan below; I'll loop in specifics and artifacts by EOD 2026-09-19.

Summary plan (owners + ETA):
- Secrets rotation + revocation (owner: Aditya Rao, Infra): rotate implicated keys, blacklist old keys, produce revocation timestamps and IAM change audit. ETA: 2026-09-17 23:59 PDT.
- Keystore hardening + repro steps (owner: Irene Choi, Security Eng): rotate KMS keys where necessary and publish an updated rotation_runbook_v1.2.md. ETA: 2026-09-18 17:00 PDT.
- Session token policy & logs (owner: Marissa Cole, Observability): enforce 15min TTLs for inference sessions, add session-start/end events to centralized logging, produce a signed sample log export (kv-cache-audit-20260914.csv or similar). ETA: 2026-09-19 12:00 PDT.
- Evidence upload & index to shared Drive (owner: Lauren Bishop): collate PDFs, runbooks, revocation CSVs, and upload to the Drive folder you shared. ETA: 2026-09-19 16:00 PDT.

If anything needs to be expedited earlier than those ETAs for your board packet, tell us which artifacts are highest priority and we can push them sooner.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Subject: Re: Pen test finding follow-up: exposed dev credentials & session logging gaps — remediation notes

Team,

Status update on the infra side (privileged creds):

What we found:
- Two S3 objects in the dev-backups bucket contained long-lived AWS access keys used by a legacy deploy helper. The keys were scoped to a cross-account role with broad s3:List* perms.

What we did (action & proof):
- Immediately revoked the two implicated access keys at 2026-09-16T23:08:12Z (AWS console IAM change event).
- Rotated the deploy helper to assume a narrowly-scoped role (policy attached) and disabled usage of long-lived keys.
- Created a rotation_runbook_v1.2.md detailing the new rotate/revoke workflow and an automated verification playbook (Ansible).
- Exported IAM audit events for the revocation window and saved to kv-cache-audit-20260914.csv (excerpt attached).

Evidence files (attached/upload plan):
- rotation_runbook_v1.2.md (Runbook + verification steps)
- kv-cache-audit-20260914.csv (IAM revocation events snippet)
- snapshot of revoked keys in AWS console (we'll upload a redacted screenshot to the Drive link)

Notes on scope & follow-ups:
- These keys were only in the dev environment and did not appear in production. We ran a search across all buckets and found no additional instances.
- We'll schedule a follow-up forensic snapshot to be delivered by 2026-09-21 in case you need deeper artifactization.

ETA for uploading the artifacts to the shared Drive: 2026-09-19 16:00 PDT.

—Aditya Rao
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Attachment: rotation_runbook_v1.2.md, kv-cache-audit-20260914.csv
From: compliance@nimbusbank.com (Laura Chen)

Cc: security@nimbusbank.com (Elliot Harrow)
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Privileged credential exposure: remediation verification plan & evidence request

Lauren —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts you uploaded to the Drive. A couple of quick clarifying asks from our compliance panel before we mark the finding as resolved:

1) For the IAM audit output, can you confirm the timezone and include an HMAC-signed export or S3 object so we can verify provenance?
2) For session token changes: can you produce a sample of raw session events (redacted PII) showing token issuance + expiry and the policy enforcement headers? A 1-2 minute excerpt is fine.

If you can provide both items by EOD 2026-09-19 (your local time), we can include them in the packet for our 2026-09-22 board review. Otherwise we may need to request a short extension.

Appreciate the collaboration — please send the additional artifacts to the Drive folder and I will confirm receipt.

Best,
Laura Chen
Senior Compliance Analyst | Nimbus Financial
